### Summaries S1: code closure digests per target, naming the parts a change touches; shared.rs's shape now resolves dynamic constants

change `xuxuymrrrqsq` · [log `472982d3adf8`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/be22079e-0c8d-41e4-ace3-12f7f213f1f9/472982d3adf890c5900c66a7c6834718f74db3d6a5b70ef27dd796b7334864fd.jsonl.gz)

lib/src/closure.rs (new) computes, for a target in a build, what its proof reads as parts with a digest each: every application method it may run (static and special calls by resolution, virtual and interface calls through every class they may dispatch to, lambda bodies, the initializers of the classes involved), every application class involved (superclass chain, superinterfaces, record components, permitted subclasses, fields with access, type, ConstantValue and annotations, class annotations), each virtual or interface call's set of dispatch targets, and the application files for a closure that touches Spring. Closure::changes names which parts differ between two builds, for the change-impact report (S3) and the proof cache's key (S2). The JDK, the tool's models and the binary are left to the canonical claim's ToolIdentity.

Found while building it: shared.rs's shape, the exact body fingerprint the brief starts from, printed a dynamic constant by its bootstrap index without resolving it. javac makes 'case Color.GREEN' in a pattern switch such a constant, so GREEN against BLUE gave equal shapes and shared::identical_closure called the versions identical: a regression check could have reported 'nothing to prove' for a changed body. A test reproduced it first; shape now resolves a dynamic constant through its bootstrap entry, recursively. The change only makes more bodies differ, so it can turn an identical-closure verdict into a proof, never the reverse. The brief's statement that shape is an exact fingerprint of a body was true except for this case.

### Summaries S2a: the claim key and the local proof cache, with adversarial invalidation tests

change `spkzmqwzmuom` · [log `ff1ae5bfb9aa`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/be22079e-0c8d-41e4-ace3-12f7f213f1f9/ff1ae5bfb9aaf5f728d7602f4c617e8b7120da67fa80e8a7f1cb3dc02ff52b25.jsonl.gz)

spec/cache.rs implements key, lookup and store. The key is the SHA-256 of the canonical claim written canonically (object keys sorted) under a projection version line. The projection knows every claim field by its path: a field it doesn't know, such as one another stream adds, makes the claim uncacheable rather than being left out of the key, and so does a computed part left empty. The cache is a local directory with one record per key. It stores only verified results and refuted ones that carry a witness; storing an unresolved result is an error, and an entry that is corrupt, for another key, or unresolved is a miss. New: closure::version_digest (a version's code as the closures of the target and of the constructors its inputs are made with), and lib/src/proof_cache.rs (the tool identity: the executable's bytes, the JDK's whole release file, the models' digest).

**Reply:**

S1 is done and committed (`xuxuymrr`), but `sync.py check` still reports one error that this branch can't clear.

**What was built:** `lib/src/closure.rs`, a new module that digests everything a proof of a target reads in one build, part by part. When two builds differ, it names exactly which parts changed. The parts are:
- each application method the target may run;
- each class involved, with its hierarchy, fields, constants and annotations;
- the set of classes each virtual or interface call may dispatch to;
- the application config files, but only for code that touches Spring.

A new subclass that overrides a dispatched method changes the closure even though no method body changed. An unrelated class, or a subclass that overrides nothing, leaves it alone.

**A soundness bug found and fixed in `shared.rs`:** the body fingerprint `shape` ignored part of what a pattern switch compiles to. So `case Color.GREEN` and `case Color.BLUE` produced the same fingerprint, and the two versions were treated as identical. A regression check could therefore have said "nothing to prove" when the code had changed. I wrote a failing test first, then fixed `shape`. The fix can only make more bodies count as different, so it may cause extra proofs but never skips one.

**Tests:**
- The new `lib/tests/summaries.rs` passes all 11 cases.
- The 183 unit tests pass. The known flaky timing test failed once and passed on its rerun.
